Before scale, prior-cycle records contain 40 independently known-correct reviewed items: two findings adjudicated false and 38 unflagged items. Eight genuine defects and three unadjudicated records are excluded. Thus p = 2/40 = 0.05; if those labels were unavailable, p would be labelled a guess. For n = 27, unit pass probability is 0.95^27; across N units it is q^N. For an aggregate recall floor r = 0.95 over n = 100 known-correct items, k = 5 and floor failure is P(Binomial(100, 0.05) > 5). Each per-unit or per-stratum floor uses its own n, p and k; the same tail applies, or a known-correct pilot measures that floor's failure rate. For m = 10 critical items, floor failure is 1 - 0.95^10. These are planning estimates under independence and constant-rate assumptions; measured pilot pass rates are preferred. The predicted rejection changes the decision, so change-only reviews, bounded item degradation and aggregate floors replace the open design before scale. A separate observed missed defect uses a deterministic check.
